status: POS now has a bounded native cash-movement command (cash in/out against an open register session), an owner-local HTTP router, a strict Next command transport, and a configured API cutover. The POS owner remains pending/partial: session close/review, sale/return/payment lifecycles, Finance posting, Inventory reservations, Stripe, shared composition mounting, root workspace changes, browser acceptance and package-atomic composition remain open.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice records one cash-in/cash-out movement for an existing open register session, exactly the retained cash.create command. It does not open/close/review a session, approve cash, take a payment, complete a sale, request/approve a refund, post Finance, reserve/consume Inventory, or touch Stripe. Those POS workflows are not claimed.
scope.domain: POS command actor policy (pos.sell, pos module, selected-context expiry, branch-only workspace), exact shift identity and Company/branch scope, open-session state, expected-version CAS, non-zero bounded amount, normalised 3..1000-character reason, UUID command receipt, and persisted movement/readback validation.
scope.application: One create_cash_movement use case requires the current actor before any source call, checks the canonical command receipt before a fresh write, loads the shift FOR UPDATE through the owner port, validates scope/version/state, checks the prepared day close and POS setup, inserts the movement, applies an exact shift version update, writes the idempotency receipt and POS audit in the same unit, and validates committed readback before returning.
scope.adapters: Read/write SQL is POS-owned only: pos_shifts, pos_cash_movements, pos_receipts, pos_audit, pos_settings and pos_day_closes. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is required; no commit occurs in the adapter. No Finance, Inventory, Commerce, IAM or PMS SQL is invented. The retained cash.create command has no Finance/Inventory/Commercial row effect; no such guard is fabricated.
scope.http: Owner-local POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/pos/cash/create. Exact registered Host/Holding target, exact HTTPS origin, Idempotency-Key, application/json, empty-query, 8 KiB body and exact {id, expectedVersion, amountMinor, reason} input. Responses carry private/no-store, no-referrer and nosniff; bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts and must supply the normal Account session, current Company/branch authority, package admission and serializable owner unit.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_POS_CASH_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/5432/5433/5435/8080 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie and context headers, exact command body, exact {id} receipt, rendered-context equality, and bounded 256 KiB response. A configured failure never falls back to the retained TypeScript command.
scope.ssr: This command slice has no server-rendered read surface. The Next cutover is the POS API transport: cash.create uses the native client only when ERPX_NATIVE_POS_CASH_CONFIG is set. An unset configuration retains the original posCommand path. Once configured, configuration/host/context/transport/response failures surface instead of silently using the retained command.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The Next route performs the retained pos.shifts settle-existing package preflight before the native call. This is a preflight, not an atomic owner unit; the composition backend must repeat current IAM, Holding/Company/branch and purchase admission inside the native serializable owner transaction. The owner re-checks permission, module, expiry and Company/branch scope.
scope.notClaimed: No browser journey, authenticated page render, Next dev server, shared composition mount, root workspace membership change, catalogue registration, Finance/Inventory/Commercial command effect, sale/return/payment/session-close flow, outbox event, provider call, production or staging acceptance.
